questions.description: Login is the core. /auth/me is a cheap way to prove the guard works and exposes the current user to handlers.
questions.recommendedAnswer: POST /auth/login (public) returning { accessToken, tokenType: 'Bearer', expiresIn }, plus GET /auth/me (protected) returning the current user.

questions.prompt: How are the hardcoded users and passwords stored?
questions.description: The user list lives in code inside modules/auth/infrastructure (behind a port, so a DB can replace it later).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Hardcoded in code with password hashes (node:crypto scrypt, no new dependency), compared in constant time. Plaintext passwords documented in AGENTS.md/.env.example comments for dev use.

options.label: In code, scrypt hashes (node:crypto, no new dep)
In code, plaintext passwords (simplest, demo only)

questions.prompt: What does a user look like, and which users should exist?
questions.recommendedAnswer: { id, username, passwordHash } with two users: admin / user. No roles for now (MVP).

options.label: id + username only, 2 users (admin, user), no roles

questions.recommendedAnswer: @nestjs/jwt (JwtService) without Passport — a small custom guard is simpler than Passport strategies.

questions.prompt: JWT secret and expiry: how does modules/auth get them?
questions.description: Rule today: modules MUST NOT import app/config (enforced by dependency-cruiser allowlist), and AGENTS.md says ask before choosing. New env vars: JWT_SECRET (required, no default, min 32 chars) and JWT_EXPIRES_IN (default e.g. 1h).
questions.recommendedAnswer: Widen the allowlist so modules may import only app/config/app-config.ts (the AppConfig token/type), inject AppConfig into JwtModule.registerAsync. Update .dependency-cruiser.mjs + AGENTS.md.

options.label: Put JWT wiring (JwtModule + guard) in app/auth/, module only calls a port
AuthModule.forRoot({ secret }) called from AppModule with config

questions.prompt: Where does @Public() live, so every module can use it?
questions.description: Health and login controllers must import it; cross-module imports are banned. Works on both method and class.
questions.recommendedAnswer: src/app/http/auth/public.decorator.ts, and add app/http/auth/ to the modules allowlist (same kind as app/http/errors: importable by presentation only). The global guard lives in modules/auth and reads the metadata via Reflector.
Health and POST /auth/login are public. Greeting becomes protected (demonstrates the guard).

questions.description: All go through the envelope as 401.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Wrong username or password → 401 InvalidCredentialsError (same message for both, no user enumeration). Missing/malformed/invalid/expired token → 401 UNAUTHORIZED, one code for all.

options.label: InvalidCredentialsError + UNAUTHORIZED (one code for all token failures)

questions.prompt: Anything else explicitly out of scope, or constraints to add?
questions.recommendedAnswer: Out: refresh tokens, logout/revocation, roles, rate limiting, user registration, Swagger auth. @CurrentUser() param decorator only if /auth/me is in scope.
